## A summary

Cleaned the data down to 52 sensor readings, trained a random forest on 70% of it with 5-fold cross-validation, 
tested it on the held-out 30%.

Results

1. Cross-validation accuracy: 99.18% (best mtry = 27)
2. Held-out validation accuracy: 99.42%
3. Out-of-sample error: 0.58%
4. Errors: 34 out of 5,885 rows

What it predicts: which of five ways a barbell curl was performed. 
A is correct form; B–E are four specific mistakes. Weakest class is C (15 misses, mostly called B). Strongest is E (1 miss).

The 20 test cases: B A B A A E D B A A B C B A E E A B B B

At 0.58% error, roughly 89% chance all 20 are right.

One caveat for the writeup: all 6 participants appear in both splits, so 0.58% is honest for these people but would be optimistic for a new person.

```{r}
#load the data.
library(caret)
library(randomForest)
set.seed(1234)

if (!dir.exists("data")) dir.create("data")

train_file <- "data/pml-training.csv"
test_file  <- "data/pml-testing.csv"

if (!file.exists(train_file)) {
        download.file("https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-training.csv",
                      train_file)
}
if (!file.exists(test_file)) {
        download.file("https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/predmachlearn/pml-testing.csv",
                      test_file)
}

training <- read.csv(train_file, na.strings = c("NA", "", "#DIV/0!"))
testing  <- read.csv(test_file,  na.strings = c("NA", "", "#DIV/0!"))

dim(training); dim(testing)
table(training$classe)

#drop book keeping columns and NA columns and near zero variances columns
training <- training[, -(1:7)]
testing  <- testing[,  -(1:7)]


na_prop <- colMeans(is.na(training))
keep    <- na_prop < 0.95
training <- training[, keep]
testing  <- testing[,  keep]


nzv <- nearZeroVar(training)
if (length(nzv) > 0) {
        training <- training[, -nzv]
        testing  <- testing[,  -nzv]
}

training$classe <- factor(training$classe)
dim(training); dim(testing)

#split and train

set.seed(1234)
inTrain   <- createDataPartition(training$classe, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
train_set <- training[inTrain, ]
valid_set <- training[-inTrain, ]

ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)

set.seed(1234)
fit_rf <- train(classe ~ ., data = train_set, method = "rf",
                trControl = ctrl, ntree = 100)

cat("\n--- Random Forest: Cross-Validation Results ---\n")
print(fit_rf)
cat("Best mtry:", fit_rf$bestTune$mtry, "\n")
cat("CV Accuracy:", round(max(fit_rf$results$Accuracy), 4), "\n")

#validation

pred_valid <- predict(fit_rf, newdata = valid_set)
cm         <- confusionMatrix(pred_valid, valid_set$classe)

cat("\n--- Validation Set Performance ---\n")
print(cm$table)
cat("Accuracy:", round(cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4), "\n")
cat("Out-of-Sample Error:", round(1 - cm$overall["Accuracy"], 4), "\n")

plot(varImp(fit_rf), top = 15)

#20 test case Prediction
pred_test <- predict(fit_rf, newdata = testing)

cat("\n--- Predictions for 20 Test Cases ---\n")
print(data.frame(problem_id = testing$problem_id, prediction = pred_test))

```
